guards.what: N1 (DORMANT): `CreatureCmd.LoseMaxHp` routes the excess current HP through the FULL damage pipeline; RunState.lose_max_hp just clamps
guards.issue: CreatureCmd.LoseMaxHp (src/Core/Commands/CreatureCmd.cs) computes an UNFLOORED newMaxHp = MaxHp - amount and, when that is below CurrentHp, deals the difference as Unblockable|Unpowered damage through the whole pipeline -- hooks, death check, Kill -- and only then calls SetMaxHp(max(1, newMaxHp)). RunState.lose_max_hp (run.py:316-321) floors max HP first and clamps `self.hp = min(self.hp, new_max)`, so no modify_hp_lost / on_damage_received / should_die fires. This is audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json guard G6, verdicted a dormant gap there, at a new out-of-combat call site -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3. DORMANT AT THIS SITE, and the argument is arithmetic rather than a population count: SetMaxHpInternal itself re-clamps `CurrentHp = Math.Min(CurrentHp, MaxHp)` (src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs), so whatever the damage pipeline does to CurrentHp on the way, the C# player still ends at min(oldHp, newMax) -- which is exactly what the sim's clamp produces. Even the one ported run-level HP-loss modifier, relic/tungsten_rod's modify_run_hp_loss (relics/tungsten_rod.py:39), is washed out by that final clamp. EXECUTED (b08-poultice): 80/80 -> 68/68, C#'s numbers. What genuinely differs is the HOOK TRAFFIC -- C# fires an unblockable-damage event that the sim does not -- and the concrete unported thing that makes it live is a relic whose ModifyHpLost or AfterDamageReceived changes run state (not just the amount), or a max-HP loss large enough to drive newMaxHp below 1, where C# kills the player and the sim floors at 1. Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CreatureCmd.cs, src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs, run.py and relics/tungsten_rod.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: ONE batched `CardCmd.Transform` of two cards vs two sequential `run.transform_card` calls -- the PileIndexSort ordering question
guards.rationale: C#'s batch Transform rolls each replacement and removes each original in list order, then SORTS the batch with PileIndexSort (CardCmd.cs:353-360, 405) -- by pile type then original index -- before the append loop, so on a Deck pile the replacements land at the end in ascending original-index order. Leafy Poultice's list is [Strike, Defend] and in the starting deck the Strike's index (0) is below the Defend's (5), so C# appends Strike-replacement then Defend-replacement -- the same order the sim's two sequential calls produce, and the same order the two RNG draws are taken in. EXECUTED in the SP2 PARITY path, which is the branch that matches C# (run.py:459-467; the legacy RL path replaces in place on purpose): the deck tail is ['breakthrough', 'colossus'] -- Strike's replacement first. NOTE this is the concrete answer to audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 56, which records PileIndexSort as a dormant gap whose trigger is 'porting any multi-card transform': Leafy Poultice IS a ported multi-card transform, and for THIS caller the orders coincide, so the dormancy holds. audit/records/relic/claws.json guard G2 is the counter-example where they do not. guards.what: N5: MaxHpVar(12m).BaseValue (LeafyPoultice.cs:17, 23) vs MAX_HP = 12 (leafy_poultice.py:27), and `isFromCard: false`
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 12 is the pinned non-ascension value, and BaseValue is the read the contract pins. `isFromCard: false` selects Unblockable|Unpowered WITHOUT ValueProp.Move for the internal damage -- i.e. Rupture-style 'lose HP from a card' triggers must NOT fire; nothing in the sim's clamp can fire them either, so the flag's effect is preserved by accident rather than by construction (see N1).

guards.what: N6: no HasUponPickupEffect override and no undo_after_obtained
guards.rationale: LeafyPoultice.cs declares only Rarity, CanonicalVars, ExtraHoverTips and AfterObtained -- no HasUponPickupEffect -- so the sim leaving has_upon_pickup_effect at the base False matches, and Ancient rarity already makes is_tradable False (relics/base.py:126-136). The absence of undo_after_obtained is NOT a C# question (nothing in the game un-picks a relic) but it is worth contrasting with relic/lees_waffle and relic/looming_fruit in this same batch, which DO implement it: Leafy Poultice mutates run state on pickup (max HP down, two deck cards transformed) and cannot be cleanly undone, because the transform is irreversible. So a conformance-runner relic swap that discards Leafy Poultice leaves the deck permanently wrong -- recorded here as a note for that stream rather than as a verdict against this unit, since no C# behaviour is being diverged from. Rule 7: relics/base.py, relics/lees_waffle.py, relics/looming_fruit.py and conformance/runner.py are not hashed by this record.
